reforms.description: Canada is promoting the application of information and communication technologies (ICT) in health care to improve quality and cost-efficiency, while also proposing the establishment of an independent, pan-Canadian agency to monitor health-care quality and provide advice on best practices to enhance accountability and improve health outcomes.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The integration of ICT in health care is expected to enhance efficiency and quality, leading to better health outcomes and potentially reducing costs.
reforms.status_evidence: Both initiatives are proposed and have not yet been implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms aim to significantly improve health care delivery and accountability, which are important but not structural changes.
reforms.source_quote: Accelerate the applications of information and communication technologies in health care, starting small-scale if necessary, resolving privacy issues and changing provider incentives.

reforms.description: The federal government has invested more than CAD10 billion since 2006 to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and build a more sustainable environment through investments in green infrastructure, energy efficiency, and clean-energy technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The investment in green technologies is expected to foster innovation and sustainability, contributing positively to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The investment has been ongoing since 2006.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant financial commitment to environmental sustainability and innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Since 2006, the Government of Canada has invested more than CAD10 billion to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and build a more sustainable environment through investments in green infrastructure, energy efficiency and clean-energy technologies.

reforms.description: The 2010 federal budget announced a comprehensive review of all federal support for research and development to improve its contribution to innovation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The review aims to enhance R&D support but the direct impact on growth is uncertain until changes are implemented.
reforms.status_evidence: The review was announced in the federal budget and is part of ongoing efforts.
reforms.importance_rationale: The review is significant as it aims to improve the effectiveness of existing R&D support mechanisms.
reforms.source_quote: The 2010 federal budget announced a comprehensive review of all federal support for research and development to improve its contribution to innovation.

reforms.description: Ontario proposed to complete the phase-out of its tax credit for Labour-Sponsored Investment Funds by 2012.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The phase-out of the tax credit may reduce incentives for investment in certain funds, potentially hindering growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The proposal has been made but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The phase-out represents a minor adjustment to existing tax policy rather than a significant reform.
reforms.source_quote: Ontario proposed to complete the phase-out of its tax credit for Labour-Sponsored Investment Funds by 2012.
